clue.text: I'm surprised about article, these days journalist is impetuous

indicators.note: about signals that the exclamation is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: oh is what someone says when surprised
the is the definite article
AD (anno Domini) marks the present era, these days
ED is the usual abbreviation for an editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: Someone reacts in surprise to a modern article by a rash journalist.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotheaded person acts rashly and on impulse, so it is a synonym for impetuous.

clue.text: Name drinking establishment that's used by bikers

parts.note: a handle is slang for a name or nickname
a bar is a place serving drinks

explanation.surface: A pub's name is chosen to suit a motorcycle crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bikers' suggests motorcyclists at a pub, but the handlebar is what any cyclist steers with.
explanation.definitionFit: The handlebar is the steering bar of a bicycle or motorbike, the part every rider grips.

clue.text: Object having watery shelled egg

parts.note: watery soup or drink is thin

indicators.note: shelled means the outer letters of the word egg are stripped off like a shell

explanation.surface: An item is described as a runny boiled egg with its shell removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shelled' strips the outer letters of EGG, leaving G.
explanation.definitionFit: A thing is any unnamed item or physical article, a general synonym for an object.

clue.text: Aged men prepared for final stage

indicators.note: prepared suggests the letters are made ready in a new order

explanation.surface: Elderly men are readied for the last phase of life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prepared' rearranges AGEDMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The endgame is the last phase of a chess game, and by extension of any process.

clue.text: Remove uniform, entering bath provided

indicators.note: entering signals that these pieces go inside the word for a bath

parts.note: a dip is a quick swim or bathe
to shed is to take off or remove
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone strips off a uniform before getting into the bath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering' puts SHEDU inside DIP.
explanation.definitionFit: Dished up, of food or anything offered, means served out, so it fits supplied or provided.

clue.text: Lovely drive, relaxed outing south for male

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for Drive in street names

indicators.note: outing means one letter is expelled from the word for relaxed
for says what letter takes the expelled one's place

parts.note: easy means relaxed or at ease

explanation.surface: A pleasant drive and an easy-going trip are being described.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outing south for male' is one instruction: throw out the south letter and put the male one in its place.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreamy is informal praise meaning delightful or gorgeous, a near-synonym for lovely.

clue.text: Settled having something to watch on TV after changing sides

indicators.note: changing sides means the left letter gives way to the right one

parts.note: a film is something to watch on television

explanation.surface: A viewer finally decides on a programme after switching seats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing sides' turns L (left) into R (right) in FILM.
explanation.definitionFit: Firm plans or arrangements are fixed and decided, so firm is a synonym for settled.

clue.text: Wooden home erected in area north of China

indicators.note: north of in a down clue places one piece above the next

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: erected in a down answer means these words are set upright, read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
china is Cockney rhyming slang (china plate) for mate, a friend

explanation.surface: A wooden house is put up in a region north of China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erected' reverses IN A to ANI. China is Cockney rhyming slang: china plate means mate.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden performance is lifeless and stiff, so inanimate, meaning without life, fits.

clue.text: Scottish engineer ignoring cold woman

indicators.note: ignoring means one letter of the engineer's name is left out

parts.note: John McAdam was the Scottish engineer who devised macadam road surfacing
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A Scottish engineer pays no attention to a chilly woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring' removes C from MCADAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Madam is a polite form of address for a woman, and can also mean a forward girl.

clue.text: Stage romance on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio signals that the word is heard, not seen

parts.note: a romance is a love story

explanation.surface: A love story is performed as a radio drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the radio' signals a homophone: STORY heard sounds like STOREY.
explanation.definitionFit: A storey is one level or floor of a building, which is a stage in its height.

clue.text: Divine being in Halifax regularly with daughter

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of these words

explanation.surface: A goddess turns up in the Yorkshire town of Halifax with her daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of 'in Halifax', NAIA. 'in' is part of the fodder, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A naiad is a water nymph of Greek myth, a minor goddess and so a divine being.

clue.text: Troublesome beads? Want this!

indicators.note: troublesome suggests the letters are in disorder and must be sorted out

explanation.surface: Annoying beads of sweat? You need this!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Troublesome' rearranges BEADSWANT. The whole clue is also the definition: beads of sweat are the trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweatband round the head or wrist soaks up perspiration, stopping drops running down.

clue.text: Traveller's gear something funny to carry in toboggan

indicators.note: to carry in means the sled holds the joke within it

parts.note: a luge is a small racing toboggan
a gag is a joke

explanation.surface: A traveller packs something amusing to take on a sledging trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Luggage is the bags and cases a traveller takes along, their travelling gear.

clue.text: March miles with figure backing political doctrine

indicators.note: backing means these two pieces together are read backwards

parts.note: six is a figure, a number

explanation.surface: Marchers cover miles while a figurehead supports their political cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns round both miles and the figure together, so the M ends up last.
explanation.definitionFit: Marxism is the political and economic theory of Karl Marx, a political doctrine.

clue.text: Reportedly dig out money for wine

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: to bore is to dig out a hole, and dough is slang for money

explanation.surface: Someone digs up cash to buy a bottle of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reportedly' signals a homophone: BORE DOUGH said aloud sounds like BORDEAUX.
explanation.definitionFit: Bordeaux is wine from the region around the French city of that name, claret among it.

clue.text: Pertinence of soldiers on enclave being mobilised

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers

indicators.note: being mobilised suggests the letters are moved into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Soldiers deploy to an enclave, and someone asks whether it is relevant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' just sets the soldiers before the rearranged enclave; 'being mobilised' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Relevance is how closely something bears on the matter at hand, a synonym for pertinence.

clue.text: Near side of yew bearing fungus

indicators.note: the near side of a word is its first letter, the end you meet first

parts.note: east is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: A fungus grows on the side of a yew tree closest to us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Near side of' takes Y from yew.
explanation.definitionFit: Yeast is a single-celled fungus used to raise bread and ferment beer.

clue.text: Upset rubbish instructor annoying person

indicators.note: upset in a down answer means turned over, so the word reads from the bottom up

parts.note: rot means nonsense, rubbish
a mentor is an adviser or instructor

explanation.surface: A teacher is irritated by nonsense from a pupil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' reverses ROT to TOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A tormentor is someone who harasses or pesters others, a person who annoys.

clue.text: Doubts moved waterfowl to vacate drought area

indicators.note: moved suggests the letters are shifted into a new order
to vacate means emptying the word of its inner letters, leaving its ends

explanation.surface: Uncertainty drives water birds out of a parched region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved' rearranges DOUBTS into DUSTBO; 'to vacate' empties waterfowl to WL.
explanation.definitionFit: A dust bowl is land made barren by drought and erosion, as in 1930s America.

clue.text: Memorial is large one occupying field

indicators.note: occupying means these letters sit inside the word for a field

parts.note: the rec, short for recreation ground, is a British playing field
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A memorial stands huge in the middle of a field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occupying' puts LI inside REC. The rec is a recreation ground, a public playing field in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is something surviving from the past, kept as a reminder or memorial of it.

clue.text: Persuaded swimmer to cover cut

indicators.note: to cover means the fish word wraps around the other piece

parts.note: a cod is a fish, a swimmer
to axe is to cut

explanation.surface: Someone was talked into getting a swimmer to hide a wound.
explanation.definitionFit: Coaxed means gently talked someone into something, a synonym for persuaded.

clue.text: Not totally exposed, back part of organ

indicators.note: not totally means the last letter of the word for exposed is dropped

parts.note: outed means publicly exposed
the rear is the back

explanation.surface: A rear part of a church organ is only partly visible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not totally' cuts OUTED to OUTE.
explanation.definitionFit: The outer ear is the visible external section of the ear, which is an organ of hearing.

clue.text: Someone you once dated, handsome model

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
handsome, as in a handsome sum, means ample

explanation.surface: A former partner turns out to be a good-looking model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'handsome' means generous here, as in a handsome profit, not good-looking.
explanation.definitionFit: An example is a pattern to follow, as is a model, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Take off from city in grip of wetness

indicators.note: in grip of means one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: damp is wetness
EC is the postcode for the City of London

explanation.surface: Someone flees a city that is held fast by rain.
explanation.walkthrough: The City of London's postcode supplies the city; 'in grip of' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To decamp is to leave suddenly or secretly, the same as to take off.

clue.text: Stray this writer's recalled feeding fruit

indicators.note: feeding means one piece goes into the other

parts.note: a date is a fruit

indicators.note: recalled means the contraction is read back the other way

parts.note: the writer refers to themself, I have, shortened

explanation.surface: An author remembers that a stray animal ate some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' reverses IVE (I've) to EVI, and 'feeding' puts it into DATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To deviate is to depart from a course, to wander off it, as does to stray.

clue.text: Pin that's blue holding nothing up

indicators.note: up in a down answer means the letters read from the bottom upwards
holding means the word for blue contains the other piece

parts.note: blue jokes are lewd
O is the figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A pin that is blue sticks up with nothing on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts O in LEWD to make LEWOD; 'up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowel is a wooden peg or pin used to join pieces of furniture.

clue.text: Something to eat and drink in part of Oxford?

indicators.note: in signals that the wine goes inside the other piece

parts.note: an Oxford is a style of shoe, and the toe is part of it
Asti is an Italian sparkling wine

explanation.surface: Students eat and drink in a college quad at Oxford.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxford looks like the university city but is a lace-up shoe; 'in' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A toastie is a toasted sandwich, a snack in British usage, so it is something to eat.

clue.text: As some might say, it's not muddy

definitions.text: As some might say, it's not
definitions.meaning: a dialect contraction of 'it ain't', written with apostrophes, meaning it is not
to muddy is to sully or spoil something

explanation.surface: Some people would insist it isn't dirty.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half gives the folksy contraction 'tain't (it ain't); with the apostrophes dropped it spells the answer, so nothing is heard, it is written.
explanation.definitionFit: To taint is to contaminate or sully, just as to muddy something is to dirty it.

clue.text: Be in wagon drunk getting wheeled home

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone gets drunk riding a wagon and is carted home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges BEINWAGON; 'getting' links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A Winnebago is a large American motorhome, literally a home on wheels.

clue.text: Value tip of writer

definitions.meaning: the purpose or worth of something, as in asking what is the use of it
the sharp end of a pen or pencil that does the writing

explanation.surface: Someone values a writer's tip.
explanation.definitionFit: Point means purpose or worth, as in 'no point', and also a sharp nib of a pen.

clue.text: Was deceitful and answered to have rep leave

indicators.note: to have someone leave is to see them out of the word for answered
leave means the three letters depart from the word

parts.note: replied means answered

explanation.surface: Someone was dishonest and responded by getting a sales rep to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to have rep leave' removes REP from REPLIED.
explanation.definitionFit: To have lied is to have told untruths, which is being deceitful.

clue.text: Material gained by Interpol yesterday

indicators.note: gained by means the answer is held within the following words

explanation.surface: The international police agency obtained some evidence yesterday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gained by' signals the answer is inside 'Interpol yesterday'.
explanation.definitionFit: Polyester is a synthetic fibre and the fabric woven from it, a material.
